c.tagline: Red phone boxes, roaring winds, and king penguins just past the last streetlamp

rides: None — no Uber, Lyft, or ride-hailing apps operate in the Falklands; call a local taxi firm directly (Stanley Cabs, Bonners Taxis, Town Taxis, or Simon's Taxis)

taxi.color: Unmarked private cars/minivans, no standard livery or roof light
taxi.fare: ~$8–12 flat fare for most trips within Stanley
taxi.fareNote: No meters — fares are fixed or agreed in advance; a transfer to/from Mount Pleasant Airport runs roughly $110–150 one-way and should be booked ahead

emergency.police: 999 (islands-wide emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance)
emergency.medical: 999 for emergencies; King Edward VII Memorial Hospital in Stanley for routine and urgent care
emergency.note: Crime is exceptionally rare; 999 is answered locally and response is fast given the small population

hood_landmark.West Stanley: Government House & the Historic Dockyard (Falkland Islands Museum)

hood_desc: The compact harbourfront core, lined with brightly painted cottages, pubs, gift shops, and the town's main jetty where cruise tenders land.

The eastern stretch of Ross Road, where the harbourfront road runs on past the town centre toward the cemetery and Whalebone Cove; a quieter waterfront address a short walk from the pubs and jetty, with several of Stanley's guest houses and self-catering flats.
The western end of town beyond the centre, where Ross Road runs out past Government House to the Historic Dockyard and the Falkland Islands Museum; quiet, residential and largely self-catering.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.pay: N/A — get around on foot, by private taxi, or rental 4x4
transit.note: There is no formal public transit in Stanley or anywhere in the Falklands; the town is small enough to walk everywhere, and local taxi firms (plus rental cars) cover trips beyond downtown, including the long haul out to Mount Pleasant Airport.

airport.name: RAF Mount Pleasant Airport (Mount Pleasant Complex)
airport.note: ~35 miles (58 km) southwest of Stanley, about 1–1.5 hours by road. Pre-booked private transfer/taxi (roughly $110–150 one-way) or a coach shuttle timed to flight arrivals; rental car pickup available at the airport terminal; no walk-up taxi rank or public bus at MPA.

tip.s: Tipping is not customary or expected anywhere in the Falkland Islands, in keeping with British practice.
tip.r: Restaurants: rounding up or adding 5–10% for standout service is appreciated but never required; taxis are never tipped.

landmarks: Christ Church Cathedral and Whalebone Arch
The world's southernmost Anglican cathedral, an 1892 brick-and-stone landmark fronted by an arch of four blue-whale jawbones, Stanley's most photographed sight.
Historic Dockyard Museum (Falkland Islands Museum)
A superb waterfront museum tracing island life, maritime disasters, wildlife and the 1982 war through restored dockyard buildings and evocative artefacts.
Gypsy Cove
A white-sand crescent just outside town where Magellanic penguins nest in the tussac grass, arguably the world's most accessible penguin colony.
Lady Elizabeth Shipwreck
The rusting iron hulk of an 1879 sailing barque grounded in Whalebone Cove, a hauntingly photogenic relic of Cape Horn's shipping graveyard.
1982 Liberation Memorial
A dignified seafront monument honouring the British forces who liberated the islands in 1982, backed by a wall naming every unit that served.
Government House
The governor's gabled 1845 residence, a quintessentially British country house improbably set amid flower gardens on the windswept South Atlantic shore.
Cape Pembroke Lighthouse
A restored 1855 cast-iron lighthouse on East Falkland's easternmost point, reached by a bracing walk past shipwreck sites and seabird colonies.
Bluff Cove Lagoon
A private nature reserve a scenic drive from Stanley, where gentoo and king penguins parade along a dazzling white beach.
Battle of the Falklands 1914 Memorial
An elegant granite monument on Ross Road commemorating the Royal Navy's decisive First World War victory over von Spee's German squadron.
Victory Green and Ross Road waterfront
Stanley's grassy harbourfront promenade, dotted with 19th-century ship mizzen masts and cannons, lined by brightly roofed cottages and pubs.

train.note: There is no railway in the Falkland Islands. Access is by air only: the weekly LATAM flight from Santiago via Punta Arenas to Mount Pleasant, and the UK Ministry of Defence airbridge from Brize Norton via Ascension Island. Mount Pleasant is about 55 km from Stanley.

bus.note: No coach routes. A shuttle bus and taxis run between Mount Pleasant airport and Stanley, timed to flights and taking about an hour on the single sealed road. Outside Stanley, travel to the outlying settlements and camp is by 4x4 or the FIGAS inter-island air service, since most tracks are unsurfaced.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry to or from the Falklands - the sea approaches are long and exposed. Stanley is a major Antarctic and South Atlantic cruise call, and small boats and charters run to Kidney Island and the wildlife sites as excursions. The Concordia Bay vehicle ferry crosses Falkland Sound between East and West Falkland.

full.name: Volunteer Point
full.blurb: Remote beach reached by 4x4 across open moorland, home to a large colony of king penguins.

notes.walk: Stanley is small and entirely walkable — the town center along Ross Road can be crossed end to end in under 20 minutes, and nearly every waterfront sight, pub, and shop sits within a few blocks of the harbour.
notes.card: Visa/Mastercard widely accepted at hotels, the Malvina House Hotel, larger restaurants, and shops in Stanley; carry FKP or GBP cash (they're interchangeable) for taxis, pubs, and small vendors — US dollars aren't used locally and must be exchanged at Stanley's bank
notes.safety: One of the safest places in the world to travel; violent crime against visitors is essentially unheard of. Extremely low; petty theft is rare, many residents leave doors unlocked, and there is no history of crime targeting tourists.
notes.religion: Christian (Anglican/Church of England, largest denomination) ~60%; Roman Catholic ~10%; Other Christian (United Free, Lutheran, Jehovah's Witness, etc.) ~10%; No religion/unaffiliated ~15%; Other faiths <5%
notes.net: Sure South Atlantic is the sole mobile operator; 4G covers Stanley and nearby areas, with prepaid SIM cards sold locally. Wi-Fi is available at hotels, guesthouses, and cafés in Stanley but is often slow and data-capped. Mobile data is costly and sold in small bundles, roughly $15–25 per GB. Connectivity runs via a 2013 subsea fibre link supplemented by satellite capacity; free wifi is limited outside hotels. Overseas roaming is very expensive; buying a local Sure SIM on arrival at Stanley or the airport is the practical option.
notes.transit: None — Stanley has no public bus, tram, or rail system
notes.transport: The only practical way in: fly to RAF Mount Pleasant Airport (MPN), about 35 mi/58 km from Stanley — served by a weekly LATAM flight from Punta Arenas, Chile (via Santiago), and a twice-weekly RAF/civilian charter from RAF Brize Norton, UK, routing via Ascension Island. No railways exist anywhere in the Falkland Islands. No scheduled public bus service in Stanley; a coach/shuttle meets international flights at Mount Pleasant to transfer passengers to Stanley. No scheduled passenger ferry service to Stanley; the harbour is a major Antarctic and South American cruise-ship stop, with passengers tendered ashore at the Public Jetty and FIPASS. Rental cars and 4x4s are available in Stanley and are essential for reaching Gypsy Cove, Volunteer Point, and other outlying sights, since most roads outside town are unpaved gravel tracks.
